pharm: Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, blocking conversion of ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides and thereby DNA synthesis (S-phase specific); in sickle cell disease induces fetal hemoglobin
quick: Individualized; oncology ~15 mg/kg/day once daily (base on actual or ideal weight, whichever is less)
May take without regard to food; swallow capsule whole - do not open/crush
Can cause fetal harm (teratogen) - avoid; use contraception
Reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <60 mL/min or ESRD; on dialysis give after dialysis
Limit - may add to GI/marrow stress; not a specific contraindication
CBC at least weekly; renal/hepatic function; uric acid; skin checks
summary: Hydroxyurea (hydroxycarbamide) is an oral antimetabolite that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase. As prescribing-information for the oncology product, it is indicated for resistant chronic myeloid leukemia and, with concurrent chemoradiation, for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (it is also widely used to reduce crises in sickle cell disease, where its labeling carries a boxed warning for myelosuppression and secondary malignancy). It causes severe myelosuppression (leukopenia first), can be teratogenic, increases the risk of secondary leukemia and skin cancers, and rarely causes cutaneous vasculitic ulcers, hemolytic anemia, macrocytosis and pulmonary toxicity. Monitor blood counts at least weekly, give folic acid prophylaxis, reduce the dose in renal impairment and counsel sun protection.
indications: Locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (excluding lip), in combination with concurrent chemoradiation
Reduction of frequency of painful crises and need for blood transfusion in sickle cell disease (per sickle-cell labeling, e.g. Droxia/Siklos)

dosage.d: Individualize; commonly ~15 mg/kg once daily, titrated to response and counts
dosage.n: Base dose on actual or ideal body weight, whichever is less

dosage.d: Per regimen in combination with concurrent radiation/chemotherapy
dosage.n: Holds drug in radioresistant S-phase / G1

dosage.c: Sickle cell disease (adult, per sickle-cell labeling)
dosage.d: Start 15 mg/kg once daily; titrate by 5 mg/kg/day every 8 weeks to max 35 mg/kg/day as counts allow
Reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <60 mL/min or ESRD
dosage.n: On dialysis days, give after dialysis

dosage.d: Interrupt/reduce dose for myelosuppression or cutaneous vasculitis

admin: Swallow capsules whole - do NOT open, break or chew (cytotoxic; avoid powder exposure)
Caregivers should wear disposable gloves and wash hands before/after handling capsules or bottle
Monitor blood counts at least once weekly; correct severe anemia before initiating
moa: Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, producing an immediate inhibition of DNA synthesis without affecting RNA or protein synthesis (S-phase specific). In head and neck cancer it is lethal to radioresistant S-phase cells and holds cells in radiosensitive G1, and impairs repair of radiation-damaged cells. In sickle cell disease it raises fetal hemoglobin (HbF).

absolute: Hypersensitivity to hydroxyurea or any formulation component
relative: Markedly depressed bone marrow function (do not initiate)
Prior radiotherapy or cytotoxic chemotherapy (greater marrow suppression)
monitor: CBC at baseline and at least weekly
Renal function and serum uric acid

preg: Hydroxyurea can cause fetal harm and is a potent teratogen in multiple animal species (embryotoxicity, fetal malformations). Advise women of the potential risk to a fetus and to avoid becoming pregnant; advise effective contraception for females and males during and after treatment.
lact: Hydroxyurea is excreted in human milk; advise women not to breastfeed during treatment because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child.
renal: Reduce the dose by 50% in patients with measured CrCl <60 mL/min or end-stage renal disease. On dialysis days, administer after hemodialysis. Monitor renal function and counts closely.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and monitor; hepatotoxicity (including fatal events) has been reported, especially with concomitant antiretrovirals in HIV.

major: Didanosine +/- stavudine (and other antiretrovirals) - fatal/non-fatal pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity and peripheral neuropathy; avoid the didanosine+stavudine combination
Live vaccines - risk of severe infection; avoid in patients on hydroxyurea
Other myelosuppressive cytotoxic agents / radiation - additive marrow suppression
moderate: Concurrent or prior radiotherapy - radiation recall (skin erythema) may occur
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food
interactions.alcohol: No specific labeled interaction; moderation advised
interactions.diagnostics: Falsely elevates urea, uric acid and lactic acid assays (interferes with urease, uricase, lactate dehydrogenase) and may falsely elevate some continuous glucose monitor readings

emergency: Signs of severe infection or bleeding (severe cytopenia)

monitoring: CBC at baseline and at least weekly throughout therapy
Renal function and serum uric acid
Skin examination for ulcers and secondary malignancies; sun protection
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; swallow capsules whole and do not open or crush them
Wear gloves and wash hands when handling capsules; keep away from children and pets
Have weekly blood tests; report fever, signs of infection, unusual bleeding or bruising promptly
Protect skin from the sun (sunscreen, protective clothing) - increased skin cancer risk
Report any non-healing skin or leg ulcers, or new breathlessness/cough
Use effective contraception (men and women) and do not breastfeed; avoid live vaccines
pk: Inhibits DNA synthesis rapidly after absorption
Peak plasma concentration 1-4 hours after oral dosing
Once-daily dosing; given continuously as effect is not sustained after discontinuation
20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep tightly closed; cytotoxic - special handling
pearls: BOXED WARNING (sickle-cell labeling, e.g. Droxia/Siklos): severe myelosuppression and increased risk of secondary malignancies - monitor counts and use the lowest effective dose
Causes severe myelosuppression - leukopenia is usually the first and most common manifestation; monitor CBC at least weekly
Teratogen and associated with secondary leukemia/skin cancers - counsel contraception and sun protection
Reduce dose 50% if CrCl <60 mL/min; avoid live vaccines; falsely elevates urea/uric acid/lactic acid lab assays
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered the same day; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take a double dose. Contact the prescriber for guidance.
overdose: Acute mucocutaneous toxicity has been reported at several times the therapeutic dose: soreness, violaceous erythema and edema of palms and soles followed by scaling, severe generalized skin hyperpigmentation and stomatitis. Management is supportive with monitoring and treatment of myelosuppression; consult toxicology.
